props.gloss_en: the priests, Levites and poor who assist at the shepherd's, the threshing floor and the slaughterhouse -- one does not give them teruma and tithe as their wage
and if they do so, they have desecrated [them]
and of them Scripture says: 'you have corrupted the covenant of Levi' (Malakhi 2:8)
and it says: 'you shall not desecrate the holy things of the children of Israel, and you shall not die' (Bamidbar 18:32)
and lest you say there is no death [for it] -- 'and you shall not die': the desecration carries death
the Sages wished to fine them, that teruma be separated on their account from [other, untithed] produce -- and they did not fine them
why not? lest one come to separate from the exempt for the obligated
and in all of them the owner has the benefit of discretion (טובת הנאה)
how so? an Israelite separated teruma from his pile, and another Israelite said to him: here is this sela, give it to my daughter's son, a priest -- permitted
if it was a priest [paying] for a priest -- forbidden
teruma has bodily sanctity; since it cannot be redeemed, one will not come to err in it
these [the priestly gifts], since they are sanctity of value, one would err in them -- [thinking] their sanctity was redeemed onto the four zuz -- and come to treat them as non-sacred
Rava: teruma of outside the Land carries no [issue] of the priest who assists at the threshing floor
Rav Chama gave it [teruma of outside the Land] to his attendant
Shmuel: teruma of outside the Land is nullified in a majority
Rabba would nullify it in a majority
and he would eat it in his days of impurity
Rav Huna b. Rav Yehoshua, when teruma wine came his way, poured two jugs of non-sacred and one of teruma and took out one; from then on, he poured one and took out one
and Shmuel said: teruma of outside the Land -- one eats as he goes and separates afterwards
and Shmuel said: teruma of outside the Land is forbidden only to one whose impurity issues from his body
and that is for eating; but touching -- we have no [objection] to it
Ravina: therefore a niddah separates challa [outside the Land] and a minor priest eats it
and if there is no minor priest, she takes it on a skewer-tip and throws it in the oven, then separates another challa, and an adult priest eats it
so that the law of challa not be forgotten
Rav Nachman to Rami bar Chama: do we then have sprinkling? [so immersion avails one impure by a corpse nothing]
Rami bar Chama to him: shall we not be concerned for the elder [Rav Amram]?
thus said Rav: one impure by a corpse immerses and eats teruma of outside the Land
and the halakha is not as he [Rav]
Mar Zutra in Rav Sheshet's name: one impure by a creeping thing immerses and eats teruma of outside the Land
and the halakha is not as he [Rav Sheshet]
